name: sync kernel module from seaweed-mono

# seaweed-mono is the source of truth for the kernel module
# (seaweed-vfs/kernel/). This repo PULLS that tree on a schedule and opens a PR
# here when it drifts. The branch and PR are created with this repo's own
# GITHUB_TOKEN, so no cross-repo write/PR permission is required — that was the
# failure mode of the old mono -> kmod push (a PAT that could push a branch but
# not open a PR). Only READ access to the private mono is external.
#
# .github/ is intentionally NOT mirrored — this repo keeps its own CI config.
#
# Reuses the MONO_SYNC_TOKEN secret (the same PAT the manual sync-to-mono uses);
# only its read access to the private seaweedfs/seaweed-mono is needed here.
# Skips silently when the secret is absent.

on:
  schedule:
    # Daily at 05:30 UTC (after the build-matrix nightly at 03:00)
    - cron: '30 5 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write       # push the sync branch on this repo
  pull-requests: write  # open the PR on this repo
  actions: write        # dispatch build-matrix to validate the sync branch

jobs:
  # Gate: emit configured=true only when the read token is present, so the sync
  # job doesn't fail with an opaque "token required" error before it is added.
  check-token:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    outputs:
      configured: ${{ steps.check.outputs.configured }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MONO_SYNC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "configured=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "MONO_SYNC_TOKEN secret not set — skipping sync." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  sync:
    needs: check-token
    if: needs.check-token.outputs.configured == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Checkout seaweedvfs-kmod
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          path: kmod

      - name: Checkout seaweed-mono kernel tree
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: seaweedfs/seaweed-mono
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_SYNC_TOKEN }}
          sparse-checkout: seaweed-vfs/kernel
          fetch-depth: 1
          path: mono

      - name: Mirror module and open a PR
        id: sync
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Mirror the module tree (source of truth) onto this repo's root.
          # Exclude .git and .github so kmod keeps its own history and CI config.
          rsync -a --delete \
            --exclude='.git/' \
            --exclude='.github/' \
            mono/seaweed-vfs/kernel/ kmod/

          cd kmod
          if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
            echo "kmod already in sync — nothing to do." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          # A single long-lived auto branch, reset from main each run so the PR
          # always shows a clean main -> current diff.
          BRANCH="auto/sync-from-mono"
          git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "sync kernel module from seaweed-mono (auto)"
          git push --force origin "$BRANCH"
          echo "branch=$BRANCH" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Reuse an open auto-sync PR if one exists; else open one (idempotent).
          if [ -z "$(gh pr list --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[].number')" ]; then
            gh pr create --base main --head "$BRANCH" \
              --title "Sync kernel module from seaweed-mono" \
              --body "Automated mirror of seaweed-mono \`seaweed-vfs/kernel/\` (the source of truth). Review and merge when the build matrix is green."
          fi

      - name: Validate the sync branch with the build matrix
        if: steps.sync.outputs.branch != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # A branch/PR created with GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger pull_request
          # or push CI (recursion guard), so kick the build matrix on the sync
          # branch explicitly — it already exposes a workflow_dispatch trigger.
          gh workflow run build-matrix.yml --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --ref "${{ steps.sync.outputs.branch }}"

name: kernel build matrix

# Compile seaweedvfs.ko against each target kernel's headers in a distro
# container. This is the source of truth for which kernels are supported: when an
# entry here breaks on a new kernel, add a shim to compat.h. Entries flagged
# `optional` are the not-yet-ported targets — they track progress without failing
# the run; promote them to required once green.
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    # Nightly at 03:00 UTC — catches distro package updates that silently bump
    # the kernel headers inside a floating image (sid, rawhide, etc.)
    - cron: '0 3 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: "build · ${{ matrix.label }}"
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.optional || false }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # --- supported (must build): 6.1 .. current ---
          - label: "6.1 LTS · Debian 12"
            expect: "6.1."
            image: debian:bookworm
            install: apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential kmod linux-headers-amd64
            kdir: /usr/src/linux-headers-*-amd64
          - label: "6.8 · Ubuntu 24.04"
            expect: "6.8."
            image: ubuntu:24.04
            install: apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential kmod linux-headers-generic
            kdir: /usr/src/linux-headers-*-generic
          - label: "6.12 · Debian 13"
            expect: "6.12."
            image: debian:trixie
            install: apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential kmod linux-headers-amd64
            kdir: /usr/src/linux-headers-*-amd64
          - label: "6.12-cloud · Debian 13"
            expect: "6.12."
            image: debian:trixie
            install: apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential kmod linux-headers-cloud-amd64
            kdir: /usr/src/linux-headers-*-cloud-amd64
          - label: "6.12 · RHEL 10"
            expect: "6.12."
            image: almalinux:10
            install: dnf install -y gcc make kmod kernel-devel
            kdir: /usr/src/kernels/*
          - label: "7.0 · Debian sid"
            image: debian:sid
            install: apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential kmod linux-headers-amd64
            kdir: /usr/src/linux-headers-*-amd64
          # --- bleeding edge (canary, non-blocking) ---
          - label: "newest · Fedora rawhide"
            image: fedora:rawhide
            install: dnf install -y gcc make kmod kernel-devel
            kdir: /usr/src/kernels/*
            optional: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: "Build in ${{ matrix.image }}"
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src -w /src ${{ matrix.image }} bash -euxc '
            ${{ matrix.install }}
            KDIR=$(ls -d ${{ matrix.kdir }} | grep -vi common | sort -V | tail -1)
            test -d "$KDIR"
            KR=$(cat "$KDIR/include/config/kernel.release" 2>/dev/null)
            echo "Building against $KR"
            # Fail if a fixed-kernel distro drifts off the version this entry
            # claims (empty expect = floating sid/rawhide, so this is a no-op).
            case "$KR" in "${{ matrix.expect }}"*) ;; *) echo "::error::expected ${{ matrix.expect }}x, got $KR"; exit 1 ;; esac
            make KDIR="$KDIR"
            modinfo seaweedvfs.ko | grep -E "vermagic|version:"
          '

# SeaweedFS kernel VFS module

[![kernel build matrix](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedvfs-kmod/actions/workflows/build-matrix.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedvfs-kmod/actions/workflows/build-matrix.yml)

`seaweedvfs` is a Linux kernel filesystem client for [SeaweedFS](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs):
a real `mount -t seaweedvfs` filesystem. The kernel module owns the VFS (inodes,
dentries, page cache) and does **zero networking**; all SeaweedFS I/O is handled
by a userspace daemon over the `/dev/seaweedvfs` character device.

This repository contains the GPL-2.0 kernel module (`seaweedvfs.ko`). The module
does not, by itself, give you a working mount — the userspace daemon that drives
`/dev/seaweedvfs` is a separate component, available with SeaweedFS.

## Supported kernels

The [build matrix CI](.github/workflows/build-matrix.yml) validates every commit
across the following kernels:

| Kernel | Distro | Status |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 6.1 LTS | Debian 12 (bookworm) | required |
| 6.8 | Ubuntu 24.04 | required |
| 6.12 | Debian 13 (trixie), RHEL 10 | required |
| 7.0 | Debian sid | required |
| newest | Fedora rawhide | canary (non-blocking) |

## License

GPL-2.0 — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Each source file carries an
`SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0` tag.

## Install

Pre-built packages are published per release at
**[seaweedfs/artifactory releases](https://github.com/seaweedfs/artifactory/releases)**.
You usually don't build by hand — pick one of these. (Each path also installs the
separate userspace `sw-kd` daemon; the module alone does not give you a mount.)

### One-line installer (easiest)

Detects your package manager (apt/dnf/yum/zypper) and arch, installs the module
(via DKMS) + the daemon, and can configure a filer in one shot:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seaweedfs/artifactory/main/seaweed-vfs/install.sh \
  | sudo FILER=10.0.0.1:18888 bash
```

Useful env vars: `SEAWEEDFS_VFS_KMOD=1` (install a precompiled `.ko` for *this*
exact kernel instead of DKMS — no toolchain needed, for fleets / hardened hosts),
`SEAWEEDFS_VFS_UPGRADE=1` (in-place upgrade), `SEAWEEDFS_VFS_RELEASE` (default
`vfs-latest`), `SEAWEEDFS_VFS_BASE_URL` (mirror your own download point).

### Pre-built packages (manual)

Three packages per release — pick **one** module package + the daemon:

| Package | What | When |
|---------|------|------|
| `seaweedfs-vfs-dkms` (noarch) | module **source**; DKMS rebuilds it per kernel | varied / changing kernels |
| `seaweedfs-vfs-kmod-<kver>` | **precompiled** `.ko` for one exact kernel | pinned-kernel fleets, no toolchain |
| `seaweedfs-vfs` (per arch) | the `sw-kd` userspace daemon | always |

```sh
# Debian / Ubuntu — DKMS module + daemon
sudo apt install ./seaweedfs-vfs-dkms_<ver>_all.deb ./seaweedfs-vfs_<ver>_amd64.deb
# ...or a precompiled module (no compiler/headers on the box):
sudo apt install --no-install-recommends \
  ./seaweedfs-vfs-kmod-$(uname -r)_<ver>_amd64.deb ./seaweedfs-vfs_<ver>_amd64.deb

# RHEL / Fedora  (on SUSE swap `dnf` -> `zypper install`)
sudo dnf install ./seaweedfs-vfs-dkms-<ver>-1.noarch.rpm ./seaweedfs-vfs-<ver>-1.x86_64.rpm
```

### Kubernetes / immutable hosts

A container shares the **host** kernel, so the module always loads there. Ready-made
node images (`ghcr.io/seaweedfs/seaweedfs-vfs`) run as a privileged DaemonSet that
loads the module, runs the daemon, and mounts on each node:

- `:<ver>` — loads the module from the host's `/lib/modules` (DKMS / kmod package).
- `:<ver>-k<kver>` — a vermagic-matching `.ko` baked in, for nodes with no package
  manager (non-Secure-Boot **Talos**, **Flatcar**, **Fedora CoreOS**).

On **Secure Boot** Talos the kernel rejects unsigned modules, so ship a signed
**Talos system extension** instead. See the SeaweedFS VFS packaging docs
(`packaging/k8s`, `packaging/talos`) for manifests and the extension build.

### Manual install of a bare `.ko`

If you have just a `seaweedvfs.ko` (built yourself, or pulled from an image):

```sh
sudo install -D seaweedvfs.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/seaweedvfs.ko
sudo depmod -a
sudo modprobe seaweedvfs               # udev then creates /dev/seaweedvfs
```

Under **Secure Boot**, `modprobe` fails with *"Key was rejected by service"* unless
the `.ko` is signed by an enrolled key — sign it with the kernel's `sign-file`
(shipped with the kernel headers at `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build/scripts/sign-file`)
using a key you `mokutil --import` once, or use the DKMS package (it signs with a
per-box MOK key and prompts you to enroll it).

## Build from source

Out-of-tree, against the running kernel's headers:

```sh
make                                  # builds seaweedvfs.ko
sudo insmod seaweedvfs.ko             # udev then creates /dev/seaweedvfs
# ... run the SeaweedFS userspace daemon, then:
sudo mount -t seaweedvfs none /mnt/seaweed
sudo rmmod seaweedvfs                 # to unload
```

Requires the kernel headers/build tree for your running kernel
(`linux-headers-$(uname -r)` on Debian/Ubuntu, `kernel-devel` on RHEL/SUSE) and a
toolchain (`make`, `gcc`). Supported kernels: 6.1 LTS → current (see table above).

### DKMS

`dkms.conf` is included so the module rebuilds automatically across kernel
upgrades:

```sh
sudo cp -r . /usr/src/seaweedfs-vfs-<version>/
sudo dkms add -m seaweedfs-vfs -v <version>
sudo dkms build -m seaweedfs-vfs -v <version>
sudo dkms install -m seaweedfs-vfs -v <version>
```

## Module parameters

- `distributed_locks=1` — route advisory (flock/POSIX) locks through the filer's
  lock service so they are honoured across mounts/clients (off by default; pair
  with the daemon's `--distributed-locks`).

Issues and the rest of SeaweedFS: <https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs>.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
# Out-of-tree kbuild for the seaweedvfs kernel module.
#
# Build against the running kernel's headers by default:
#   make            # build seaweedvfs.ko
#   make clean
#   make KDIR=/lib/modules/<ver>/build   # build against a specific kernel

obj-m += seaweedvfs.o

KDIR ?= /lib/modules/$(shell uname -r)/build
PWD  := $(shell pwd)

all: compat-config.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD) modules

# Compat feature probes (ZFS-style): build a tiny module against the target
# kernel to detect an API, then emit a HAVE_* #define into compat-config.h,
# which compat.h includes. Robust across kernel versions and distro backports,
# where LINUX_VERSION_CODE lies. Each probe is one .c in compat-probes/.
#
# probe(basename,DEFINE): build compat-probes/<basename>.c alone (via a one-line
# generated Kbuild) and emit #define DEFINE into compat-config.h if it compiles.
probe = printf 'obj-m := $(1).o\n' > compat-probes/Kbuild; \
	$(MAKE) -s -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD)/compat-probes modules >/dev/null 2>&1 \
		&& echo "\#define $(2) 1" >> compat-config.h || true

compat-config.h: FORCE
	@echo "/* generated by 'make' feature probes — do not edit or commit */" > $@
	@$(call probe,inode_state_read,HAVE_INODE_STATE_READ)
	@$(call probe,file_lock_core,HAVE_FILE_LOCK_CORE)
	@$(call probe,set_default_d_op,HAVE_SET_DEFAULT_D_OP)
	@$(call probe,d_revalidate_dir,HAVE_D_REVALIDATE_DIR)
	@$(call probe,lookup_noperm,HAVE_LOOKUP_NOPERM)
	@rm -f compat-probes/Kbuild compat-probes/*.o compat-probes/*.ko \
		compat-probes/*.mod* compat-probes/.*.cmd \
		compat-probes/modules.order compat-probes/Module.symvers 2>/dev/null || true

clean:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD) clean
	@rm -f compat-config.h

FORCE:
.PHONY: all clean FORCE
